Kamalanathan : Petitioner
 versus
 Sakthivel : Respondent
 Prayer: Petition filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of Ind
 aside the fair and decretal order passed by the Sub Court, Uthangar
 in Ia No. 04 of 2023 in Os No. 312 of 2022 dated 22.02.2024
For Petitioner : Mr.P.M.Jayachandran

Order 
This civil revision petition arises against the dismissal of the petition filed for rejection of plaint.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.
O.S.No.312 of 2022 was filed by one Sakthivel/respondent.
He claims that the property belonged to his great-grandmother, Ramiyammal.
She passed away in the year 1970.
She had only one son namely Kaliyappa Naicker, who was the plaintiff's grandfather.
Kaliyappa Naicker had three sons namely Raji Naidu, Nataraj and Sampath.
The civil revision petitioner/third defendant and the respondent/plaintiff are the sons of Raji Naidu and Pattammal.
3. Arraying his mother and seven siblings as defendants, the respondent/plaintiff presented a suit for partition.
It was his case that the third defendant had obtained a settlement deed from Raji Naidu on 14.09.2006, without his knowledge.

He would state that the said settlement deed is null and void and would claim the following reliefs in the suit:

1 a. Passing a preliminary decree for partition and Separate Possession of 1/9th share of plaintiff into the suit A Schedule properties.
b. Appoint a Court Commissioner, directing him to divide the suit A Schedule properties into 9 equal shares by metes and bounds with reference to good and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis bad soil, allot one such share to plaintiff pass a final decree accordingly and put the plaintiff in separate possession of the same.

sentences.text: c. Granting permanent injunction restraining defendants 3, 9 to 11 from in any manner alienating or encumbering the suit properties to any third parties.

Declaring the fraudulent gift settlement deed dated 14.09.2006 bearing Doc.No.1502 of 2006 executed by Raji Naidu in favour the Kamalanathan (3rd defendant) as null and void;
g. Declaring the sham and nominal partition deed dated 15.03.2017 bearing Doc.No.516/2017 entered into between the defendants 3, 10 & 11 as null and void; https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.
On being served with summons, the third defendant took out an application for rejection of the plaint.
This application was received in I.A.No.4 of 2023.

5. The plea of the third defendant is that the property belonged absolutely to Raji Naidu on account of the partition that had been entered into between Raji Naidu and his brothers, and Raji Naidu in exercise of his power of ownership had settled the property in favour of the third defendant.
Therefore, the third defendant became the absolute owner of the property.
Hence, he would plead that the property is not open for the aforesaid reliefs.
6. The learned Trial Judge dismissed the application.
Hence, the revision.
7. Heard Mr.P.M.Jayachandran for the civil revision petitioner. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 8.

Mr.P.M.Jayachandran would submit that on the partition between Raji Naidu and his brothers,
the subject property became an absolute property of the Raji Nadu and he could have alienated the property in favour of any one.
Raji Naidu had alienated the property in favour of the third defendant and therefore, the present suit is not maintainable.
He would refer to Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act in order to plead that Raji Naidu is the absolute owner of the property.

sentences.text: I have carefully considered the submissions of Mr.P.M.Jayachandran.
10. Whether the settlement deed is true, genuine, and had been acted upon is a matter which requires evidence.
For the mere fact that the third defendant is projecting a settlement deed, the Court cannot accept the same to be true and genuine, especially when the plaintiff seeks to repurdiate it.

11. In terms of the Transfer of Property Act, a settlement deed requires attestation and any document which requires attestation would have to be https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis proved in terms of Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Mr.P.M.Jayachandran's case would have been easier, had the plaintiff accepted the settlement deed.
This is because the proviso to Section 68 makes it clear that if a settlement deed is accepted, then the proof for such document is dispensed with.
Unfortunately, that is not the situation today.
12. The plaintiff has denied the settlement deed and has sought for a declaration that it is null and void and not binding on him, which implies that he is denying it.
Therefore, the third defendant would necessarily have to comply with the requirements of Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act to substantiate the plea of title that has been projected by him.
If the matter requires evidence and is a triable issue, obviously the plaint cannot be rejected.
13. In the light of the above discussion, I do not find any reason to interfere.
The civil revision petition is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
